review.body:
<!-- rivetari-judge-review round=1 -->
### Rivetari judge · round 1 · approve

#### Acceptance
- A1: met — generateSignal/generatePiecewise, pacer output, rawValue/toRaw; tests cover length, the 1.5/3.0 ±3 pattern and the raw mapping.
- A2: met — PACED_GOLDEN has all six profiles; the early shift is derived from timingSdBreathFraction; tests assert each defining property.
- A3: met — Paced and open faults present. The lost-span test checks flatness, single-sample spikes and an exact match outside the span. The ±100% check relies on artifactLimitPctOfMax ≥ 100.
- A4: met — mulberry32 lives in analysis; three seeded noise kinds; same and different seed, zero SD, and per-sample SD within 10% are all tested.
- A5: met — Test passes for the default timings at 20 Hz. See the defect: expected values are not exact for off-grid knot times.
- A6: unverified — Constants come from config.ts and index.ts re-exports synth. No lint, typecheck or test run output was provided with the diff.

<details><summary>5 suggestion(s), non-blocking</summary>

- Calibration 'expected' A100/midline silently disagree with the samples when knot times are off the sample grid `src/lib/analysis/synth.ts:415` _(downgraded: no reproduction confirmed: The finding rests on acceptance criterion A5 ('known exactly' against the samples), but no A5 text is given, so it doesn't exist here. The arithmetic (a 12.5 Hz grid misses the 5 s peak) is real, but nothing in this diff promises that expectedA100 and expectedMidline match the sample extremes. They are documented only as derived from the knot levels, and the default 20 Hz path aligns.)_ — In generateCalibration, throw a RangeError when any knot time × sampleRateHz is not an integer (within a tiny tolerance). Alternatively, compute peaks, troughs and the expected values from the rendered samples at the knot indices.
- Piecewise join is discontinuous at the marker `src/lib/analysis/synth.ts:209` — Bridge the segments with a half-cosine from the last knot before the marker to the first knot after it, or document that markers should fall on matching transitions.
- A first segment with fromS > 0 is silently treated as starting at 0 `src/lib/analysis/synth.ts:198` — Throw a RangeError if ordered[0].fromS !== 0, or document the behaviour.
- Spike magnitude is asserted against artifactLimitPctOfMax rather than ±100% `src/lib/analysis/synth.test.ts` — Also assert Math.abs(v) > 100 for every spike.
- Golden-check factors (0.35, 1.8, 9, 0.5) are typed into synth.ts `src/lib/analysis/synth.ts:266` — Move GOLDEN_FACTORS into config.ts if the Appendix owns them.

</details>

_claude-opus-5-5 · 2 call(s) · Claude reviews, humans merge._

suggestions.title: Calibration 'expected' A100/midline silently disagree with the samples when knot times are off the sample grid
suggestions.detail: generateCalibration places peaks and troughs at knot times restS + k·(inhaleS+exhaleS) (+inhaleS), but samples only exist at i / sampleRateHz. When a knot time × sampleRateHz is not an integer, no sample lands on the peak or trough. The recording's extremes then sit below the stated peaks and above the stated troughs. expectedA100 and expectedMidline are still reported from the knot levels as if they were exact. A5 promises values that are 'known exactly' against the generated samples, and B1-2 calibration tests built on non-default timings or rates would get golden values off by much more than 1e-9, with no error raised. The defaults at 20 Hz happen to align, which is the only case the test covers.
suggestions.repro: generateCalibration({ a100: 2.2, midline: 2.3, sampleRateHz: 12.5 }): the first peak knot is at t = 5 s, and 5 × 12.5 = 62.5, so no sample falls on it. Math.max(...rec.raw) < Math.max(...rec.peaks), and the A100 computed from the sample extremes ≠ rec.expectedA100 = 2.2 beyond 1e-9. Likewise inhaleS: 3.03 at 20 Hz.
suggestions.fix: In generateCalibration, throw a RangeError when any knot time × sampleRateHz is not an integer (within a tiny tolerance). Alternatively, compute peaks, troughs and the expected values from the rendered samples at the knot indices.
suggestions.downgraded: no reproduction confirmed: The finding rests on acceptance criterion A5 ('known exactly' against the samples), but no A5 text is given, so it doesn't exist here. The arithmetic (a 12.5 Hz grid misses the 5 s peak) is real, but nothing in this diff promises that expectedA100 and expectedMidline match the sample extremes. They are documented only as derived from the knot levels, and the default 20 Hz path aligns.

suggestions.title: Piecewise join is discontinuous at the marker
suggestions.detail: Each segment renders from its own knot set, so the signal jumps at fromS whenever the two patterns are at different phases or levels. Later transition detectors may count the step as a spurious transition.
suggestions.repro: generatePiecewise([{fromS:0,pattern:pattern15},{fromS:30,pattern:{inhaleS:2,exhaleS:2,peakPct:6,troughPct:-6}}], …): user[599] and user[600] differ by several % in one sample.
suggestions.fix: Bridge the segments with a half-cosine from the last knot before the marker to the first knot after it, or document that markers should fall on matching transitions.

suggestions.title: A first segment with fromS > 0 is silently treated as starting at 0
suggestions.detail: startS is forced to 0 for the earliest segment regardless of its fromS, which can hide a caller mistake.
suggestions.repro: generatePiecewise([{fromS:10,pattern}], {durationS:20,…}) renders the pattern from t = 0.
suggestions.fix: Throw a RangeError if ordered[0].fromS !== 0, or document the behaviour.

suggestions.title: Spike magnitude is asserted against artifactLimitPctOfMax rather than ±100%
suggestions.detail: A3 requires every spike to be beyond ±100% of max. The per-spike assertion compares against FIXED_CONSTANTS.artifactLimitPctOfMax, and only `some` spikes are checked against 100. That is equivalent only if the constant is 100.
suggestions.repro: If artifactLimitPctOfMax were below 100/1.2, spikes scaled by 1.2 would pass the test while being under 100%.
suggestions.fix: Also assert Math.abs(v) > 100 for every spike.

suggestions.title: Golden-check factors (0.35, 1.8, 9, 0.5) are typed into synth.ts
suggestions.detail: These are Appendix golden-pattern numbers. A6 only names pacer depth, the timing SD fraction and the pacer half cycles, which do come from config.ts. Moving the rest there would keep a single source of truth.
suggestions.fix: Move GOLDEN_FACTORS into config.ts if the Appendix owns them.
